sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the Middle Durance valley, in the southern Provence region (SE France), between the towns of Digne (to the north) and Manosque (to the south), north-east of Aix-en-Provence. This source marks the transition between the Valensole Plateau (to the east), which belongs to the most external portion of the Alpine fronts, and the Panneau Provencale (to the west).
Recent instrumental seismicity in the region is generally low (below Mw 3.5), with hypocentral depths within the uppermost 15 km of the crust. However, remarkable historical seismicity affected the overall Provence (Champion et al., 2000; Baroux et al, 2001; 2003). In particular, four earthquakes have occurred along the Middle Durance valley in 1509, 1708, 18212 and 1913 (Champion et al., 2000).
The Middle Durance is a slow active fault system that has been associated with moderate-size historical earthquakes. Based on earthquake data and rupture modeling, Aochi et al. (2006) maintain that this fault system is made of a number of segments, thinner toward the north, with left-lateral oblique kinematics, generally dipping to the north-west.
The strike and dip of this Source are based on geological and geophysical data. The rake, indicative of oblique reverse faulting, is inferred from seismological data. The minimum and maximum depth are based on seismological data. The slip rate is based on various geological and geodetic data.
